09:00.headline: Before you pay for a showcase
09:00.topic: Do/don't: get numbers first, pick events where his levels' coaches attend, don't pay for every invite, follow up after
09:00.caption:
Before you write the next showcase check, ask one question: who will actually be watching?

Showcases can help. They can also add up fast. A few habits make the money go further:

✅ Get his numbers first: exit velo, 60 time, velo, grades. Knowing where they stack up tells you which levels to aim for.
✅ Pick events where coaches from those levels show up. Ask the organizer which programs attended last time.
❌ Don't pay for every invite that lands in your inbox. More events isn't the same as better exposure.
❌ Don't skip the follow-up. A short email to the coaches you hoped would see him keeps the event working after it ends.

Which showcase lesson did your family learn the hard way? 👇

13:00.headline: 3 steps to follow up with a coach
13:00.topic: How-to: follow up with a college coach after a camp (timing, what stood out, updated numbers + video)
13:00.caption:
The camp is over. Now what?

Many families wait for the coach to reach out first. Often the more useful move is a short, polite follow-up from your player.

⚾ Email within a week, while the camp is still fresh.
⚾ Mention one thing that stood out: a drill, a piece of feedback, something he took away.
⚾ Include updated numbers and a short video link, so the coach can see where he is today.

Keep it brief and in his own words. It also shows a coach he can handle his own communication.
